characters.description: A seventh-iteration survivor and rare Blademaster training as a Warden alongside his drake partner, Gris. He chooses a class perk that channels the knowledge of Earth's swordmasters, hoping disciplined growth will prepare him for dangers beyond ordinary Warden work.
characters.name: Zacharia Gardner

characters.description: Zach's drake partner, training companion, and practical adviser. He cautions Zach to reserve essence for equipment and daily costs, and believes the Wardens are preparing them for future leadership.
characters.name: Gris

characters.description: The newly installed head of the Twilight Melody Sect and an exceptionally advanced cultivator. He repeatedly prevents his eyes from regenerating so he can improve his resonance-based perception while preparing his weakened sect for pressure from its neighbors.
characters.name: Ryun Nacht

characters.description: Ryun's second-in-command and a central administrator of the Twilight Melody Sect. She helps manage its rule and political problems while Ryun concentrates on cultivation.
characters.name: Anrosh Kesh

characters.description: An experienced adviser who handles the Twilight Melody Sect's business, including the sale of valuable assets. He warns that neighboring powers may test the sect after its abrupt change of leadership.
characters.name: Eerv Ji Van

characters.description: A disabled but deeply knowledgeable cultivation mentor. Unable to demonstrate techniques herself, she teaches Ryun through theory, careful observation, and exacting lessons about control and balanced attributes.
characters.name: Tali

characters.description: Ryun's awakened sword. During his cultivation training, she helps him gather the shadow-aspected essence he needs to fill his core.
characters.name: Kagehime

characters.description: The more candid of two twin operatives traveling through Ryun's territory under a concealed purpose. She investigates the new sect leader while he permits the sisters' activities on the condition that they harm no one under his protection.
characters.name: Nayra Ornn

characters.description: Nayra's cautious twin and the leader of their covert group. She conceals their larger operation while assessing Ryun, his rule, and the risks of working within his territory.
characters.name: Reyla Ornn

characters.description: A Karora Warden, jeweler, and advanced skill user. He explains that high-tier skills demand genuine self-knowledge and warns Zach that rapid advancement can permanently bind part of a person's identity into a skill.
characters.name: Ferret

characters.description: Zach's partner in Haven and Rayleigh's adoptive mother. She shares a home with them while Zach's duties as a protector draw him toward a crisis on the eastern frontier.
characters.name: Linda

characters.description: The adopted daughter of Zach and Linda. Orphaned when the Framework arrived, she now lives with them in Haven.
characters.name: Rayleigh

characters.description: A woman loved by Ryun and remembered as Zach's friend. Ryun says her murder by the eastern governor's forces drove his retaliation against the city.
characters.name: Melody

characters.description: Zach's newly bonded awakened sword. Mistral grants wind-based attacks, control over nearby air, and sharper hearing, while expressing clear preferences about how the weapon should be treated.
characters.name: Mistral

characters.description: A quiet Warden archivist assigned to assist Zach with the city's serial-murder investigation. She approaches the work methodically and becomes his partner in reviewing old cases for patterns the earlier inquiry missed.
characters.name: Quell

characters.description: Anrosh's young daughter. Ryun gives her his cultivation path, which manifests through her inherited Absolute Cold aspect, and her elders choose gradual training without adding a class.
characters.name: Kri

characters.description: A Framework broker appearing in Ryun's fragmented dreams of the former aspects of True Death. The Dealmaker offers the dying beings a form of survival that would alter what they are.
characters.name: the Dealmaker

characters.description: The elderly Heavenly Realm head of the neighboring Last Ember Sect. He agrees to meet Ryun on neutral ground as the approaching monster swarm creates pressure for cooperation.
characters.name: Emberhorn

characters.description: An Earth swordmaster spirit carried within Zach's class perk. Zach learns to manifest him briefly as a nonphysical instructor and begins receiving focused sword training.
characters.name: Sasaki Kojiro

characters.description: Ryun's contracted wolf partner. Separated from his pack, Ereclaw is uncertain what purpose remains for him and turns to Ryun to discuss his future.
characters.name: Ereclaw

characters.description: The shapeshifter behind Quell's identity and the killings attributed to the Night Horror. She tells Zach that her feelings for him were real, even as their confrontation forces him to judge her actions and the danger she presents.
characters.name: Neha

characters.description: A chained eighteen-ringed shade imprisoned deep in the ethereal structure. The shade traps Zach in a constructed dream and tells him that escape requires confronting himself.
characters.name: the chained yeti shade

characters.description: A soul weapon and metal right hand forcibly made from Mistral and Zach's essence-siphoning dagger. Its creation breaks Zach's bond with his awakened sword and leaves him with an unfamiliar weapon while trapped in the ethereal prison.
characters.name: Shade Reaver

characters.description: The final living captive in a soul-draining ritual and the daughter of the mining expedition's high ranker. Once Zach frees her, she uses stone-breaking attacks and seismic awareness to help them flee the prison.
characters.name: Jen

recaps.ending:
Ryun has answered Emberhorn's betrayal by taking his city, but the victory follows Eerv's death and Anrosh's severe soul injury. Anrosh recovers, receives Kagehime, and shares practical leadership of the Twilight Melody Sect with Nayra. Ryun orders them to retake Venoran, then leaves with Ereclaw to gather void essence and prepare for the Centennial Tournament. Kri is safe at Wolf's Grove. Reyla remains apart from Nayra, although their class advancement is still linked.

Zach escapes the ethereal prison after freeing Jen from a soul-draining ritual. Restoration elixirs regrow his severed leg, but it remains numb and requires a long recovery. The prison's ruling spirit gravely wounds Jen's father, so the breach is sealed rather than conquered. The yeti runelord who transformed Mistral into Shade Reaver is also at large. Reunited with Neha, Zach chooses the Planar Warrior evolution and joins Jen's father's group to gain access to its dungeons. Zach and Ryun remain separated, and Zach no longer accepts responsibility for Ryun's crimes.
recaps.in_short: Zach pursues skill mastery and Warden service while preparing for a future reckoning with Ryun. His investigation of the Night Horror costs Gris his life and exposes Quell as the shapeshifter Neha. Zach kills Neha with the gauntlet's fire, but she is alive and traveling with him when his story resumes. Together they direct her violent compulsions toward wanted criminals. Ryun strengthens the Twilight Melody Sect against a monster swarm, only for Emberhorn to betray the defense. Eerv dies, Anrosh survives a soul injury, and Ryun conquers Emberhorn's city before leaving Anrosh and Nayra to rule while he trains with Ereclaw. Zach's later expedition into an ethereal prison strands him among powerful spirits. A freed yeti runelord remakes Mistral into Shade Reaver and escapes. Zach fills the weapon with new forms, rescues Jen, and reaches safety after losing a leg. The restored leg remains numb. He becomes a Planar Warrior and leaves with Neha and Jen's father's group, while the sealed prison and escaped runelord remain unresolved threats.

recaps.text: Previously: Zacharia Gardner and Ryun Nacht are surviving rankers from the seventh iteration of Earth. They were once friends, but their paths separated after the Framework transformed their world. Zach became a protector associated with Haven and later entered Warden service with his drake partner, Gris. Ryun pursued cultivation to extraordinary heights and eventually took control of the Twilight Melody Sect in the Infinite Realm. Their unresolved history, including Ryun's violence and Zach's determination to confront him, continues to shape both men's choices.

Zach advances his rare Blademaster class, choosing a perk that briefly grants the combined guidance of Earth's swordmasters. He also reaches peak Foundation cultivation, but decides that skills may offer his best route to greater power. Gris advises him to balance advancement against the expense of equipment and Warden life.

Ryun, now head of the weakened Twilight Melody Sect, trains under Tali while deliberately remaining blind to improve his resonance-based perception. Eerv and Anrosh manage sect affairs, and the covert twins Reyla and Nayra assess Ryun's intentions. He promises ordinary members freedom to keep what they earn, while warning the twins that their hidden work must not harm anyone under his protection.

A past crisis in Haven sends Zach to investigate a city destroyed after its governor abused nearby settlements. The killer proves to be Ryun. Ryun says the governor's forces tortured prisoners and murdered Melody, prompting his retaliation. Zach accepts the crimes against Ryun's people but condemns the killing of innocents. Ryun rejects Haven's authority and refuses a public judgment. Zach does not force an arrest, and the former friends part with their relationship broken.

Zach bonds with his awakened sword, Mistral, gaining wind attacks, improved hearing, and limited control of nearby air. That hearing draws him into a serial-murder investigation after a powerful golden-eyed killer escapes him. Quell, a Warden archivist, joins the case. Zach also prepares a five-person team for the Abyssal Deep, invests in new armor, and carries an essence-siphoning dagger despite Gris's concern.

Within the Twilight Melody Sect, Ryun advances his resonance skill and continues consolidating his rule. Reyla receives an order to return from her hidden faction, but Nayra chooses to remain with Ryun, splitting the twins. Ryun then gives Anrosh's daughter Kri his Path of the Final End. Her Absolute Cold aspect changes its techniques, and her elders decide that she should cultivate steadily without taking a class.

A Category 3 monster swarm is moving toward the sect's lands. Nayra has formally joined the sect and teaches spear fighting at Wolf's Grove. Ryun leaves to scout the horde while Anrosh and Eerv prepare contact with the neighboring Last Ember Sect. The sect has only months to strengthen its warriors and arrange a defense.

Zach's team clears the first five floors of the Abyssal Deep. The expedition tests its formation against swarms, traps, golems, ice creatures, and a goblin fortress. Zach loses a hand to a boss but the healer regenerates it. On the final floor, his Greater Strike becomes Flurry Strikes, giving him his first self-directed skill evolution. The rest of the team rejects another deliberately underleveled run, revealing a growing difference between Zach's appetite for risk and theirs.

Ryun discovers that the approaching swarm is led by a Legendary Tier 10 thunderbird whose defense can turn aside his strongest cut. Anrosh and Eerv meet Emberhorn, the elderly Heavenly Realm leader of the Last Ember Sect, and arrange a neutral meeting. The threat now exceeds what Ryun expected his sect to face alone.

Gris encourages Zach to ask Quell out, and their relationship deepens. Quell describes losing her parents during forced combat advancement and questions whether institutions restrict exceptional people as well as protect society. Zach shares his determination to find Ryun. He then spends nearly all his essence to reach level 120, evolving from Blademaster into an Ethereal Warrior with a customizable soul-damaging blade.

Zach accepts a ten-year secrecy contract with Ferret, who teaches that a perfect skill must contain an authentic part of its user. Past events then reveal the depth of Zach and Ryun's rupture: after Melody's death, Ryun suffered memory loss and escalating dissociation, claimed territory around New Dallas, and attacked the city. He killed Linda and Zach's child without recognizing them.

In the present, Ryun spends the sect's resources to reach the Heavenly Realm before the swarm. He and Emberhorn agree to a joint defense, though neither side fully trusts the other. Ryun also gains Astral Eyes, allowing him to perceive essence, cores, conduits, and class pathways.

Zach develops Perfect Tempest Dance Style by binding his commitment to protect loved ones into the skill. An ethereal gnaw cat then identifies a building used by the Night Horror to change shape. During surveillance, the suspect kills Gris and another Warden before Zach can intervene. The shapeshifter is Neha, and she reveals that Quell was one of her assumed identities. Although she says their relationship was genuine, Zach decides not to repeat his failure with Ryun and kills her with the gauntlet's fire. He leaves the city after learning that the Wardens knowingly allowed the lethal operation to continue as a test of him.

The monster swarm reaches the allied city. Ryun and his summoned avatar hold the horde outside the wall while the two sects defend within. After Ryun wounds the thunderbird leader, Emberhorn turns a massive fire attack on both of them, breaches the wall, and reveals his betrayal. Ryun kills the wounded swarm leader, but monsters pour into the city.

Anrosh attacks Emberhorn and is struck down. Eerv kills Emberhorn's son and wounds the retreating leader, but suffers fatal soul damage. Ryun cannot save him. Before dying, Eerv entrusts his awakened spear to Ryun. Ryun evolves Resonance Sense into a perfect skill and finds Anrosh, whose related injury is survivable but slow to heal. Ereclaw gets Kri and a small group of warriors toward Wolf's Grove, while Nayra survives and helps hunt the scattered swarm.

After Anrosh recovers, Ryun strengthens himself and leads a coordinated assault on Emberhorn's city. Anrosh and Nayra seize its gates and barracks while Ereclaw slips toward the palace. The betrayal is confirmed as premeditated. Ereclaw kills Emberhorn, and Ryun claims the city and its territory for the Twilight Melody Sect.

Reyla returns to her influential family after being expelled from the Order of Warbringers. Her parents begin rebuilding her strength, but her advancement remains tied to Nayra's because Nayra became the lead twin. Reyla is forced to follow the class evolutions Nayra selects, eventually gaining the same unusual dawnfire-linked path, while still refusing to contact her sister.

Zach is later traveling with Neha as her romantic partner. They direct her violent compulsions toward criminals carrying death warrants, rescue captives, and use bounties to fund advancement. After killing a rogue who concealed his true power, they recover valuable equipment and enough essence for Zach to reach level 180. He evolves into a Phantom Slayer and gains the ability to open a temporary fissure into the ethereal realm. They move to the underground city of Dal D'Vor in search of stronger work.

Ryun finds that his void-aspected body can survive beyond the world's spatial boundary, giving him access to dangerous high-tier void essence. He transfers Kagehime to Anrosh, leaves the sect's practical rule to Anrosh and Nayra, and orders them to retake Venoran. He and Ereclaw depart to train for the Centennial Tournament.

Zach and Neha accept a contract to reopen an ethereal rift after spirits abduct members of a mining expedition. They join a high ranker's rescue team and enter an immense prison-like structure. Powerful spirits and shades overwhelm the expedition, and Zach is knocked into the prison depths, separated from Neha and unable to reopen his fissure until its cooldown ends.

A chained eighteen-ringed yeti shade traps Zach in repeated dream lives centered on Ryun and Earth's destruction. Zach breaks the loop by rejecting the belief that Ryun's choices were his responsibility. Nearly three weeks have passed when he wakes. The former runelord claims that an earlier Framework civilization was later repurposed as monsters. Zach frees it after receiving a promise of help, but the shade betrays him, dismantles his equipment, and forcibly combines Mistral with his essence dagger to create Shade Reaver before escaping.

Mistral's bond and voice are gone. Shade Reaver can instead absorb aspects from spirits and shades. Zach advances through the prison, killing wardens and draining imprisoned shades to gain Wind, Darkness, Blood, Venom, Frost, and Fire forms. By level 233 he has stronger ethereal defenses and short-range teleportation, but alerted wardens are converging on him.

Zach kills an eight-ringed sphinx shade and gains Shade Reaver's final form, Time. He abandons plans to hunt anything stronger and discovers prison spirits draining the souls of living captives. The last survivor is Jen, daughter of the expedition's high ranker. Zach frees her, and her mining abilities help them flee through the prison. He releases other shades as a diversion, uses dangerous time powers against their pursuers, and loses a leg before opening a fissure to safety.

Several days later, Zach wakes with the leg regrown by restoration elixirs, though it remains numb and will take months to recover. Jen's father reports that the prison's ruling spirit gravely injured him and cannot be defeated by the present expedition. He seals the breach and rewards Zach for saving Jen. The freed yeti runelord also remains at large.

Neha is alive but had to be restrained after losing control when she believed Zach was dead. They reunite and decide to travel with Jen's father's group for access to its dungeons. Zach postpones a narrow anti-spirit path and instead evolves into a level-239 Planar Warrior. Elsewhere, Ryun trains with Ereclaw while Anrosh and Nayra lead the Twilight Melody Sect and prepare to reclaim Venoran.

characters.description: A reserved business analyst and dedicated amateur archer who trusts his intuition but usually avoids notice. He is sharing an elevator with several coworkers when the system announces Earth's initiation and sends him into the unknown.
characters.name: Jake

characters.description: The full name of the reserved analyst introduced as Jake. After awakening in the system's introduction room, he chooses Archer as his tutorial class and receives the skills and starter equipment needed to enter the Great Forest.
characters.name: Jake Thayne

characters.description: Jake's wealthy, charismatic supervisor and friend. His confidence and social ease make him a natural focus for the coworkers caught in the initiation, in contrast with Jake's preference for remaining in the background.
characters.name: Jacob

characters.description: An HR coworker traveling with Jake's elevator group when the initiation begins. Jake is attracted to her, although her interest appears to be directed toward Jacob.
characters.name: Caroline

characters.description: A physically imposing but gentle member of the elevator group with ties to Jacob's upbringing. His size suggests strength, but his calm manner distinguishes him from a conventional enforcer.
characters.name: Bertram

characters.description: The office receptionist and one of the coworkers caught in the same elevator as Jake. She is present with her husband when the initiation begins.
characters.name: Joanna

characters.description: A coworker from research and development who reunites with Jake on the tutorial platform. He selects Archer, making him the ten-person group's second ranged weapon specialist alongside the much more practiced Jake.
characters.name: Casper

characters.description: The commanding leader of a much larger armed survivor force. He presents his organization as a cooperative merger, but speaks for it alone and makes clear that Caroline's service as a healer is the central condition of his offer.
characters.name: Richard

characters.description: A member of Jake's original survivor group who receives a serious bite during a hunt. Caroline's healing and a health potion stabilize the injury, demonstrating both the danger of routine encounters and the group's dependence on medical supplies.
characters.name: Theodore

characters.description: Richard's trusted lieutenant, an experienced archer formerly employed by Richard's private security firm. He leads a seven-person stealth unit sent after Jake and remains outside Jake's immediate perception while directing the pursuit.
characters.name: Nicholas

characters.description: An unusually powerful teenage caster living at the edge of Richard's growing camp. He keeps his independence, searches for mana potions, and regards the settlement chiefly in terms of what its healers, crafters, and supplies can provide.
characters.name: Lone teen caster

characters.description: A coworker from the original tutorial group whose death is reported as the conflict between the two large survivor camps worsens. His loss is part of the mounting evidence that the supposed reprisals are consuming both factions.
characters.name: Dennis

characters.description: A participant associated with Richard's camp who is reported dead amid the escalating conflict with the rival settlement. Her death is one of several casualties attributed to the cycle of attacks between the two groups.
characters.name: Lena

characters.description: A caster in Richard's settlement whose class develops a frost specialization. He is among the camp members advancing into more defined combat roles while the conflict with the rival faction intensifies.
characters.name: Ahmed

characters.description: A Metal Savant embedded in Richard's camp who has secretly murdered parties from both major factions and arranged the evidence to prolong their war. He hides behind a frightened public manner while pursuing his goal of becoming the tutorial's sole survivor.
characters.name: William

characters.description: An ex-military survivor who leads the large camp opposing Richard's organization. His faction believes Richard's side is responsible for the continuing attacks, unaware that William is engineering violence against both settlements.
characters.name: Hayden

characters.description: The poison-focused namesake of the alchemist profession offered inside Jake's challenge dungeon. Accepting that legacy grants Jake specialized alchemical abilities but also leaves him with a dormant toxin he must cure within thirty days.
characters.name: Malefic Viper

characters.description: Casper's girlfriend, identified only after she has been murdered during the faction conflict. Her death becomes the personal loss that determines Casper's response to the killer and to the tutorial itself.
characters.name: Lyra

characters.description: The deity who has protected the diminished Malefic Order during the Malefic Viper's long absence. The Viper's return places this guardian in a position to help the order respond to its patron's renewed activity.
characters.name: Lord Protector

characters.description: The unnamed highest-ranking mortal leader of the reduced Malefic Order. An obelisk signaling the Malefic Viper's return summons her to respond to her patron's renewed activity.
characters.name: Malefic Order hallmaster

characters.description: A bearded smith who privately approaches William. He invokes their separate divine connections and opens a discussion about a secret alliance.
characters.name: Bearded smith

characters.description: The smith who equips William for the coming war and asks him to avenge family members killed by Richard's people. Hermann gives his remaining life and power to transform the armor into a soulbound Epic legacy bearing his name.
characters.name: Hermann Schmidt

characters.description: A light caster and Hayden's former second-in-command who organizes the rival camp's last defense. He counters Richard's mass assault with concealed fighters and false defectors after taking on much of the faction's planning.
characters.name: Desmond

characters.description: An unnamed, wounded rapier fighter who remains beside Desmond after their faction's defending force is reduced to the two of them.
characters.name: Wounded rapier fighter

characters.description: A smiling stranger who appears after William collapses from the destruction of Richard's force. He uses a crystal to prevent William from dying, then departs without revealing who he is.
characters.name: Unidentified man

characters.description: The leader of the badgers in Badger's Den and Jake's final target within the dungeon. She waits in the boss cavern with several Alpha Venomfang Badgers and is stronger than her subordinates.
characters.name: Den Mother

characters.description: A primordial deity who invites Jacob into her realm after his class evolves into Augur of Hope. She recruits him as a future speaker and offers her Greater Blessing in exchange for his service.
characters.name: Holy Mother

characters.description: Jake's former university roommate, recalled during a dream about an old betrayal. Jake remembers discovering that Andrew had become involved with Madeline while she was still Jake's girlfriend.
characters.name: Andrew

characters.description: Jake's former girlfriend, seen through his dream of a painful university memory. Her affair with Andrew left Jake with a betrayal he had avoided fully confronting.
characters.name: Madeline

characters.description: A hidden presence uses Andrew's likeness to enter Jake's dream and encourage distrust of Jacob. Its nature remains unknown when the Malefic Viper challenges the projection.
characters.name: Dream intruder

characters.description: The unseen ruler of four beast lords that guard separate dungeons. The Beast Lords quest requires defeating all four lords to force their king to appear.
characters.name: Unseen beast king

recaps.ending: Jake clears Badger's Den alone after killing its Alpha Venomfang Badgers and the level 82 Den Mother. He leaves with the rare dagger Venomfang, the Den Mother's poison gland, upgraded titles, and one of four required victories in The Beast Lords quest. He expects the other mountain dungeons to hold the remaining lords, whose deaths will draw out their unseen king. The survivor factions outside have collapsed. Richard, Caroline, Hayden, Hermann Schmidt, and Desmond are dead. William survives his destruction of Richard's force only because an unidentified man intervenes, and he remains hostile toward Jake and Richard's surviving followers. Jacob lives as the Holy Mother's newly blessed Augur of Hope, sustaining the remaining group's morale while concealing painful truths. Joanna and Bertram are last known alive, while Casper has left the tutorial as a young undead. The Malefic Viper has ended his seclusion, regards Jake as a friend, and has prompted the Malefic Order to take an interest in Jake. The force behind an attempted manipulation of Jake's dream remains unidentified.
recaps.in_short: When Earth enters the system, office analyst and archer Jake is sent into a lethal forest tutorial with his coworkers. His exceptional instincts awaken as the Bloodline of the Primal Hunter, and he leaves the group after Richard coerces them into a larger settlement and sends Nicholas to kill him. A solo challenge makes Jake an alchemist tied to the god known as the Malefic Viper, whose blessing helps him cure the dungeon's poison and begin combining archery with toxins. Meanwhile William secretly engineers a war between the survivor factions. Richard and Caroline later help ambush Jake, ending his interest in reconciliation. William ultimately betrays Richard, kills Caroline and Richard, and destroys most of the organized survivors, though an unidentified man preserves his life. Jacob survives and becomes the Holy Mother's blessed Augur of Hope. Jake remains in the inner area, clears Badger's Den by killing its level 82 Den Mother, and begins a quest to defeat three more beast lords before confronting their unseen king.

recaps.text:
Earth is absorbed into the system, and Jake enters a sixty-three-day forest tutorial with coworkers from his elevator. He chooses Archer, while Jacob becomes the group's leader, Bertram its main defender, Caroline its healer, and the others fill additional combat roles. Jake's long experience with a bow immediately makes him their strongest hunter. The first battles bring food and levels but also cost Joanna part of a leg, creating conflict when Jacob blames Jake's independent attack for the injury.

Jake begins testing an unexplained ability to sense danger. During his solitary night watch, three other initiates ambush him for equipment and tutorial points. His awareness expands under pressure, allowing him to kill all three. The system identifies the awakened ability as the Bloodline of the Primal Hunter, which strengthens his instincts, perception, and awareness of nearby threats. Jake gains substantial levels and a new title, but the emotional aftermath isolates him from the horrified group. Only after the fight does he fully confront that his opponents were human.

Jake pushes his coworkers to hunt rather than hide, but Richard soon arrives with a larger armed organization and makes Caroline's services as a healer a condition of cooperation. Jake leaves alone after warning Richard not to mistreat the others. Richard nevertheless sends Nicholas and six stealth fighters to remove him. Jake ambushes the squad, kills Nicholas and most of the pursuers, and releases one survivor to carry a warning. Richard suspends further action, while Jake begins hunting deeper in the forest by himself.

Solo combat raises Jake's levels and teaches him the limits of both his bloodline and his physical recovery. He finds hidden magical lockboxes, acquiring self-repairing bracers and improving his cloak. Avoiding other humans, he searches for stronger prey and worthwhile rewards. A cave leads him to a solo challenge dungeon available only to high-scoring initiates below level ten who lack a profession. Jake meets every condition and enters, surrendering any certainty about what waits inside.

The challenge dungeon removes Jake's equipment and ordinary skills, then subjects him to corrosive traps and symbolic crossings. His bloodline continues to function despite the restrictions. By choosing a dangerous route associated with a wyvern rather than an offered safe path, he earns access to a hidden area and witnesses a creature's progression from snake to dragon.

A poisoned pedestal offers Jake a profession linked to the Malefic Viper. He accepts and becomes a poison-specialized alchemist, but must cure the dormant toxin within thirty days. Working from the dungeon's laboratory, garden, and library, he learns to brew mana and health potions, studies toxins by consuming them, and creates a hemotoxic poison suitable for coating weapons. His growing profession complements his archery but does not yet solve the lethal deadline. Continued alchemy carries his race to its evolution threshold, and he becomes a Human F. The evolution also strengthens his Bloodline of the Primal Hunter, after which he invests heavily in perception and resumes the search for a cure.

Outside the dungeon, Richard's settlement expands into a fortified community while deaths mount in a supposed war with Hayden's rival camp. Joanna's race evolution restores her leg and she leads the crafters. Jacob becomes an administrator, Caroline becomes his partner, and Casper develops as a trapper. The conflict is not what either faction believes: William, a teenage Metal Savant within Richard's camp, has been killing groups from both sides and arranging the evidence to sustain the war.

Jake continues alchemy under his poison deadline, creating common Necrotic Poison and earning a superior profession evolution. The evolution brings him face to face with the Malefic Viper, revealed as the god who created the dungeon and its legacy. The Viper grants Jake a True Blessing, conceals the scale of Jake's achievements from wider notice, and treats him with unusual personal favor. Jake returns from that meeting with new abilities and substantial gains, but he remains confined in the dungeon and must still cure its dormant poison before the deadline.

Jake prepares a volatile poison-based cure as the dungeon deadline approaches. When the implanted toxin activates, he drinks the mixture and survives the struggle between its opposing energies and his own vitality. The cleared dungeon rewards him with rare boots, a storage necklace, and new titles. He packs its portable books, equipment, ingredients, and plants before the timer expires, then returns to the tutorial forest. His long absence has left him separated from both major survivor groups and unaware of much of their internal collapse.

Within the faction conflict, William continues exploiting mistrust and isolated fighters. Casper discovers that William murdered Lyra, Casper's girlfriend. Rather than accept an ordinary death or continue within the tutorial, Casper performs a ritual transformation. His living body dies, but he becomes a young undead and is removed from the tutorial under the authority of unidentified observers. Casper deliberately leaves William alive to remember what happened. The apparent death therefore marks an exit and transformation rather than a simple killing, while William remains embedded among survivors and the larger war continues.

Jake advances through increasingly dangerous hunts, refining his poison-assisted fighting style and moving toward the tutorial's inner area. He develops Powershot and continues to favor difficult solo opponents as the fastest route to growth. His connection to the Malefic Viper remains hidden from the human factions.

Richard learns enough about William's violence to understand that the teenager is a killer, but keeps him as a useful weapon against Hayden's camp while planning to dispose of him afterward. This choice preserves the threat inside Richard's own organization. Far beyond the tutorial, an obelisk signals the Malefic Viper's return and summons the diminished Malefic Order's mortal hallmaster. Lord Protector, the deity who guarded the order during its patron's absence, is also positioned to respond to the return.

Richard uses Jake's earlier clashes with both camps to portray him as the hidden murderer driving the war. The story gives Richard and Hayden a common target while concealing William's responsibility. Jacob attempts to reopen contact with Jake, but the meeting is part of an ambush. Caroline knowingly assists Richard's plan, even as Jacob's own participation remains uncertain.

Jake escapes the coordinated attack by breaking into the inner area, where the tutorial's boundary had previously kept the human factions out. Hayden critically wounds him with a fiery spear, but Jake reaches the barrier and crosses it. Isolated and badly injured in the inner area, Jake faces three high-level raptors without support.

Jake recovers in the inner area, evolves his combat class into Ambitious Hunter, and continues hunting high-level beasts. Outside, Jacob confronts Caroline, who admits her part in the ambush. A smith named Hermann Schmidt secretly allies with William after Richard's people kill Hermann's family. Hermann sacrifices his life to transform William's armor into a soulbound Epic legacy, and William accepts the obligation to avenge him.

Richard marches nearly two hundred people against the remnants of Hayden's faction, seeking control of almost every surviving human. Desmond's defenders spring an organized counterattack, but their force is destroyed and Desmond dies in a failed attempt to take Richard with him. William then betrays Richard's side and kills Caroline. Protected by Hermann's armor, he fights Richard's remaining elites and unleashes a vortex of battlefield metal that destroys nearly everyone, including Richard. William collapses critically injured after vowing further revenge. An unidentified man uses a crystal to keep him alive. The organized survivor order is left effectively annihilated.

Jake sees the tutorial population settle at only forty-nine survivors and decides not to return to the outer camps. He clears a resource-rich valley, upgrades his quiver, acquires a frost-enchanted short sword, and develops Splitting Arrow. His exploration leads to Badger's Den, a dungeon intended for as many as five people, which he enters alone.

Jake fights through packs of Venomfang Badgers while replenishing arrows, potions, and poison between encounters. The dungeon's Alpha Venomfang Badger proves fast enough to counter his usual movement and resistant enough to remove poisoned flesh. During the battle, Jake learns to support Powershot with mana as well as stamina, destroying his old bow but evolving the attack into the rare Infused Powershot. He kills the level seventy-one alpha through accumulated wounds, poison, and blood loss. At class level forty he also gains Mark of the Ambitious Hunter, a covert tracking and damage ability. The Den Mother remains ahead as the dungeon's true objective.

Jacob finds the aftermath of William's massacre, confirms Caroline's death, and chooses not to kill the unconscious William. His failing combat path evolves into Augur of Hope, a class built around guidance and support. The Holy Mother recruits him, grants him a Greater Blessing, and positions him as a future speaker. Jacob returns with new abilities for sustaining others while keeping painful information from the remaining survivors.

In Badger's Den, Jake kills the additional alphas around the final chamber and successfully creates a common hemotoxic poison. An attempted dream manipulation uses the appearance of his former roommate Andrew, but Jake recognizes the intrusion and the Malefic Viper drives the outside influence away. Jake then marks the Den Mother, counters its poison, summoned alphas, barrier, and healing, and kills the level eighty-two beast with poisoned arrows and Infused Powershot. The solo clear advances his dungeon titles and yields Venomfang, a rare dagger, along with armor and a valuable poison gland. A new quest identifies the Den Mother as one of four beast lords. Jake leaves with one lord defeated and turns toward the remaining dungeons that will force their unseen king to appear.

characters.description: The Malefic Viper's Chosen and leader of a five-member C-grade party entering Nevermore. Jake combines archery, alchemy, poison, arcane magic, and unusually sharp perception, often taking responsibility for scouting and navigation.
characters.name: Jake Thayne

characters.description: Jake's wind-affinity companion and a member of his Nevermore party. Her speed, unusual movement, and wind senses make her an exceptional scout, especially when hostile terrain or limited visibility restricts the rest of the group.
characters.name: Sylphie

characters.description: A disciplined swordsman in Jake's Nevermore party. He brings exceptional blade technique, a measured outlook, and a willingness to adapt his methods to unfamiliar environments while pursuing continual improvement in his chosen path.
characters.name: Sword Saint

characters.description: A unique life form in Jake's party who fights with force and soul powers. His broad telepathic and tracking capabilities help the group coordinate.
characters.name: Fallen King

characters.description: Haven's administrator while Jake is in Nevermore. She acts as his trusted territorial manager and oversees his territory in his absence.
characters.name: Miranda

characters.description: The primordial patron behind Jake and the head of the Malefic Order. His standing shapes how powerful outsiders respond to Jake and his companions, while his legacy supplies many of the alchemical and poisonous abilities central to Jake's path.
characters.name: Malefic Viper

characters.description: A Grand Elder of the Malefic Order and mentor to Jake's former disciple. He supports her advancement and guides her healing and alchemical path.
characters.name: Duskleaf

characters.description: A dryad druid, healer, and plant commander in Jake's party. She begins the run by creating hundreds of vine soldiers to search the first floor, showing both broad battlefield support and precise control over plant life.
characters.name: Dina

characters.description: A newly C-grade dungeon engineer aligned with the Risen. His class analyzes dungeon functions and reveals information unavailable to ordinary challengers, earning him a place in an elite party despite combat not being his main specialty.
characters.name: Casper

characters.description: The leader of the elite Risen Nevermore party that Casper joins as its dungeon engineer.
characters.name: Ghost King

characters.description: A Valhall-associated Rune Maiden selected for an elite Nevermore party. Her record of one hundred consecutive arena victories marks her as an unusually formidable entrant from the new universe and establishes that she earned her place through combat strength.
characters.name: Carmen

characters.description: The host and creator of the labyrinth spanning Nevermore floors 31 through 40. He offers several difficulty routes, monitors challengers closely, and demonstrates knowledge that extends beyond his manifested body.
characters.name: Minaga

characters.description: The personal name the Sword Saint gives when meeting Minaga. Miyamoto is the same disciplined swordsman who entered the labyrinth with Jake, Dina, Sylphie, and the Fallen King, and he approaches its unfamiliar trials as opportunities to refine his blade.
characters.name: Miyamoto

characters.description: A level-270 foe released when Jake's party opens a sealed gate by taking a direct route through the labyrinth.
characters.name: Demon Lord

characters.description: A mortally wounded knight who confronted the released Demon Lord. He blames Jake's party for the release, and a curse emerges from his body after he dies.
characters.name: Knight of Light's Dawn

characters.description: A demonic cult leader conducting a mass-sacrifice ascension ritual on floor 32. She commands demon guardians, and defeating her before the ritual finishes completes the floor's related bonus objective.
characters.name: Prime Summoner

characters.description: A royal mage whom the party frees from a cult prison on floor 32. He identifies the escaped Demon Lord as Gubrothas, explains that the Mage Court sealed him five centuries earlier, and offers the party a stone that can temporarily seal the demon's sword.
characters.name: Old Royal Mage

characters.description: An ancient Demon Lord released when Jake's party opens a sealed route through Minaga's labyrinth. The Old Royal Mage identifies him as a foe sealed by the Mage Court five centuries earlier, and his escape makes him the central enemy of the connected scenario.
characters.name: Gubrothas

characters.description: An old demon seeking peace on floor 34. He asks the visitors to gain entry to Gubrothas's locked stronghold.
characters.name: Old Demon

characters.description: The half-demon leader of the cult that summoned Gubrothas and the strongest figure outside the sealed castle. She alone can open the castle and stands above the competing mistresses on the floor.
characters.name: Prime Consort

characters.description: A beastkin mistress aligned with the Prime Consort on floor 34. She recruits Jake into that faction and directs him to gain supporters, influence rival mistresses, or remove opposition.
characters.name: Ninth Mistress

characters.description: A politically neutral mistress who opposes Gubrothas. Sylphie reaches her while the party searches for allies, scrolls, and a route into the sealed castle.
characters.name: Second Mistress

characters.description: The unaffiliated leader of the guards in the floor-34 city. His faction is independent of the competing mistresses, and the Fallen King learns that he holds one of the three secret scrolls.
characters.name: Guard Captain

characters.description: The respected leader of nearly a million human and scalekin survivors transferred to Earth. Miranda asks him to organize plans for their autonomous resettlement and nullifies his slave contract.
characters.name: Former Knight Commander

characters.description: A former enslaved worker studying alchemy and healing under Duskleaf. She cultivates rare plants and pursues C-grade so she can return to free and protect her family and clan.
characters.name: Duskleaf's Disciple

characters.description: A Holy Church augur and fellow Earthling encountered on Minaga's city layer. He belongs to another competing Nevermore party.
characters.name: Jacob

characters.description: A powerful Earthling healer aligned with a Tao sect and another bloodline patriarch. His extraordinary life energy attracts Eternal Hunger's attention when he joins the gathering on Minaga's city layer.
characters.name: Aaron

characters.description: The leader of a separate Nevermore party. His group loses a prospective recruit in a Demon Lord encounter and must find a replacement before continuing, leaving his team temporarily depleted in the growing record contest.
characters.name: Caleb

characters.description: The Vespernat Hive Queen. Returning to the Endless Empire, she calls Jake her sire, claims powerful lineage treasures, and maintains loyalty to both him and the Empire despite internal suspicion.
characters.name: Vesperia

characters.description: A divine observer who watches a recording of Jake's floor-40 victory alongside the Malefic Viper and Minaga. The Worm God agrees that wider powers should not learn enough about Jake's bloodline to manipulate him through political or personal relationships.
characters.name: Worm God

characters.description: A long-established half-elf space mage ruling the Enlightened Republic on floor 41. He acknowledges the world's plague, has lived on the planet for more than two thousand years, and offers Jake's party a difficult means of leaving the scenario.
characters.name: Enlightened Republic Lord Protector

characters.description: The former leader of a fourth faction on floor 41 and a specialist connected to the plague afflicting the world. Records in the ruined republic indicate that she survived underground after her faction's defeat.
characters.name: Dark Witch

characters.description: A senior Malefic Order authority who tests Duskleaf's disciple before her C-grade evolution. He accepts her commitment to her mentor while making clear that formal access to the Order's secrets carries severe and potentially lethal obligations.
characters.name: Order Lord Protector

characters.description: The new identity of Duskleaf's former enslaved disciple after her perfect C-grade evolution into a high elf. Dawnleaf becomes Duskleaf's principal disciple and begins a path centered on nurturing plant and treasure life.
characters.name: Dawnleaf

recaps.ending: The book closes with the Nevermore run still in progress. Jake, Dina, Sylphie, Miyamoto, and the Fallen King have cleared floor 46 intact after establishing the record through floor 40, killing an independent Minaga clone, and earning a final-score multiplier. Their cure of floor 41 removes the karmic plague and saves the Dark Witch, although she remains badly injured and must seek her own way out. Jake advances his arcane path through Protean Arrow and Arcane Supremacy, but his party has fallen several thousand points behind the current leader. Elsewhere, Vesperia remains with the Endless Empire under Minaga's scrutiny, Miranda manages Haven's strained resettlement, and Carmen conceals her friendly link to Jake from her party. Dawnleaf completes a perfect C-grade evolution and formally becomes Duskleaf's principal disciple. Minaga's interest in Jake, Vesperia, and Miyamoto remains unexplained, while the Malefic Viper and the Order Lord Protector anticipate a wider convergence of dangerous powers.
recaps.in_short: Jake Thayne leads Dina, Sylphie, Miyamoto, and the Fallen King through Nevermore, rapidly clearing the early floors before entering Minaga's ten-floor labyrinth. They permanently destroy Gubrothas, endure a long city-floor toll, and defeat the true-ending boss on floor 40 without losing a member. The defeated Minaga is revealed as a real clone of the god called the All-God Legion. On floor 41, the party discovers a karmic plague that has stripped a world's natives of agency. They overthrow its ruling factions, restore the Dark Witch, transfer the plague into a false core, and destroy it while saving her. Jake develops Protean Arrow, chooses Arcane Supremacy, and helps the group clear through floor 46, though another team takes the leaderboard lead. Outside the run, Miranda struggles with mass resettlement on Earth, Vesperia settles into the Endless Empire under Minaga's attention, and Duskleaf's former disciple evolves into Dawnleaf.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne became the Malefic Viper's Chosen and built Haven into a growing center of power on Earth. His close circle includes Sylphie, Miranda, Caleb, and the figures now joining him for Nevermore: the Sword Saint, the Fallen King, and Dina. Jake's unusual perception, archery, alchemy, poison, and arcane abilities have made him both exceptionally capable and politically significant. Sylphie provides speed and wind senses, while the Fallen King brings force, soul magic, and communication abilities. The Vespernat Hive Queen Vesperia regards Jake as her sire, linking him to the Endless Empire, while Miranda manages his territory during his absence and faces the continuing work of integrating displaced people. Duskleaf has taken an interest in Jake's former disciple and supports her advancement. Jake and his companions now enter Nevermore as C-grades, seeking growth, records, and the rewards of the multiverse's most famous dungeon while Earth continues changing behind them.

Jake's five-person party clears Nevermore's first thirty floors at exceptional speed. Each member proves valuable in different environments: Dina commands plants and defeats an optional sky monarch alone, Sylphie dominates the ocean and wind-aligned challenges, the Fallen King supplies communication and force magic, and the Sword Saint continually adapts his swordsmanship. Jake's perception and tracking repeatedly expose hidden routes and objectives. The party leaves some marginal bonuses behind to preserve its pace, reaches successive city layers, and arrives at floor 31 only a few hundred points below the existing record. They expect the next section to provide their first serious resistance. Other elite entrants are gathering. Casper joins a Risen party as its dungeon engineer, Carmen enters with a Valhall-aligned group after an extraordinary arena record, and further faction teams prepare their own runs. On Earth, Miranda reaches C-grade and begins confronting the housing, governance, and political demands of receiving vast displaced populations.

Floor 31 begins Minaga's Labyrinth, a connected challenge spanning floors 31 through 40. Jake's party chooses Archmage difficulty, then uses his perception to cut through deceptive fog and bypass much of the intended maze. Their direct route releases a sealed Demon Lord. They defeat it in the first encounter, but it escapes and remains part of the continuing scenario. On floor 32, the party avoids a curse, rescues an imprisoned Old Royal Mage, stops every demonic ritual, and rejects both a specialized anti-demon item and outside aid. The mage identifies the escaped enemy as Gubrothas, an ancient Demon Lord sealed five centuries earlier. Floor 33 replaces the maze with guarded prisoner rooms. Dina protects captives and destroys sacrifice formations before each attack, allowing the group to free enough prisoners for the bonus objective without deaths. Elsewhere, a rival Chosen attempts to read Minaga's emotions and finds the host's mind too vast and composite to assess safely.

The party finishes the prisoner floor and infiltrates a cult-controlled city on floor 34. They ally with the Second Mistress, who opposes Gubrothas, while Jake gains private access to the Prime Consort by presenting carefully selected truths about his bloodline. The Prime Consort reveals that three scrolls control the Demon Lord's heart, armor, and crown, then attempts to drug Jake for a fatal ritual. Jake reverses the poisoning contest and delivers her to the Second Mistress. The Fallen King kills the guard captain for another scroll, and the party secures all three. Minaga later confirms that the Second Mistress is the surviving princess of the kingdom Gubrothas destroyed. The group earns emergency escape talismans, retains the scrolls, and decides to deliberately empower Gubrothas before confronting him.

The battle with Gubrothas escalates through his empowered artifacts and summoned tower demons. Jake corrupts the floating heart, forcing the Demon Lord to destroy it and release its stored fire. Dina holds the collapsing battlefield together, Sylphie controls heat and the flying sword, the Fallen King breaks summoned formations, and Miyamoto helps suppress the fire domain. After the party clears the supporting enemies, Jake repeatedly weakens one point of the armor with poison and corruption. The group restrains Gubrothas, Jake breaches the armor, and Miyamoto bisects him. Gubrothas moves his body, soul, and artifacts into his sword to escape, but the party stops its teleportation. Jake sends Eternal Shadow through Eternal Hunger and destroys him permanently. The achievement places the party in the Nevermore point lead. Minaga's city floor then blocks further progress with a personal coin toll that cannot be paid by teammates, beginning a lengthy earning campaign for every member.

While Jake's party spends more than a year crafting, fighting, and working for Minaga Coins, competing teams advance. Carmen completes a dangerous Valhall ritual and becomes a living Rune Maiden. A void-touched independent party enters the record race, Vesperia reaches the Endless Empire and claims lineage treasures, and Caleb loses a prospective recruit during his party's Demon Lord encounter. Jake meets Carmen, Casper, Caleb, Jacob, and Aaron on the city floor. Aaron explains that he seeks to overcome mortality by healing the effects of time and gives Jake research for the Malefic Viper's judgment. On Earth, Miranda frees a former knight commander's transferred people and asks them to shape their own settlement. Jake eventually reaches his toll and works on the Puzzle Box of the Seeker while waiting for Sylphie and the Fallen King. Once all five can pay, the party enters floor 36 and begins the final section of Minaga's labyrinth on Archmage difficulty.

Jake's party clears floors 36 through 39 by choosing the hardest rooms while exploiting shortcuts, hidden routes, and unusual solutions. Floor 40 presents Minaga himself as the true-ending boss. The encounter removes defeated members rather than killing them, and the best bonus requires all five to remain. Minaga uses layered elemental, spatial, physical, and constellation magic, then separates the party into individual trials. He gives Miyamoto a punishing lesson in the conceptual use of a blade while clones challenge the others. In the final phases, Jake survives alone until his companions escape their spatial prisons. The reunited party breaks Minaga's defenses, restrains him, and enables Jake to implant an ancient poison made with the Malefic Viper's venom. Minaga's cosmic form collapses and he detonates, but Dina's defense preserves everyone. The party clears floor 40 with no member defeated and gains a twenty-five percent final-score multiplier. A stronger Minaga then appears and reveals that he is a god.

Minaga explains that the boss the party killed was an independent, fully real clone. His clones share knowledge but possess separate souls and records, making his true existence exceptionally difficult to end. He rewards the Fallen King with the defeated clone's soul core, Dina with an ancestral branch, Miyamoto with a sword-training formation, Sylphie with a mythical dream nest, and Jake with a cradle that can cultivate one soul flame. The Malefic Viper later identifies Minaga as the All-God Legion and worries about his growing interest in Jake. Casper's party also completes the floor-40 true ending, although it suffers defeats and earns a smaller multiplier. After recovering, Jake's group reaches the next city layer with 54,373 points, establishing the record through floor 40. They learn that floors 41 onward are larger and more valuable, then enter a planetary scenario where three factions compete and the stated task is to determine the world's fate.

On floor 41, the party discovers that the native population carries a karmic plague that compels obedience, prevents lies, and makes established rulers defend the existing order. Jake rejects the offered exit and divides the party to dismantle the Enlightened Republic, Beast Folk Alliance, and Risen Kingdom. He kills the republic's Lord Protector while the others destroy the remaining leadership and living seals. Evidence leads them beneath the world to the Dark Witch and the plague-saturated planetary core. The Fallen King purges her corruption, revealing that rival factions betrayed her earlier attempt to cleanse the world. She helps construct a mimic core that draws the plague out of the real one, but destroying it should kill every infected person, including her. Jake uses the Malefic Viper's abilities, his own defensive time-slowing effect, and the party's help to redirect the destruction. The karmic plague is eliminated while the Dark Witch survives, badly injured but sane. A gateway appears and floor 41 is complete.

The party leaves the recovering Dark Witch with records that may help her escape and receives major rewards, including another final-score multiplier for saving her during the cure. Floor 42 teaches the protections surrounding bloodline holders. Jake's party shields a young heir from imperial abduction, exposes a coup, and sees a god enforce the prohibition against coercive recruitment and reproduction. Jake then reaches his C-grade skill choices. For his profession, he selects Arcane Curse Manifestation, allowing him to stabilize curse fragments for alchemy and rituals. On Earth, Miranda continues managing crowded settlements, newly freed populations, and the arrival of reusable Nevermore access. Jake's class selection offers stronger arrow techniques or a deeper commitment to his unique affinity. He chooses Arcane Supremacy, which reforges his body and soul around arcane energy. His arcane barriers, attacks, and freeform magic improve, while direct use of other combat energies becomes harder unless mixed with arcane power.

Jake's party completes floors 43 and 44 through careful identification rather than indiscriminate destruction, then reaches a divine-authority scenario on floor 45. Jake invokes his status as the Malefic Viper's Chosen, prompting two gods to waive the intended route and lower the barrier to the exit. The unusually fast and peaceful clear yields 17,000 points, but the group learns that another team now leads by several thousand. Minaga visits Vesperia in the Endless Empire and extends his scrutiny from Jake to the sole Vespernat true royal. On floor 46, the party splits to kill four beast kings. Jake and Sylphie finish their targets first, and Miyamoto negotiates a peaceful departure when the frightened local kingdom turns against them. The five continue deeper into Nevermore intact. Outside the dungeon, Carmen hides her existing friendship with Jake behind a false Valhall assignment. Duskleaf's former enslaved disciple completes a perfect C-grade evolution, becomes the high elf Dawnleaf, and formally accepts the obligations of serving as his principal disciple.

characters.description: The Malefic Viper's Chosen leads a five-person party through Nevermore. After the group completes floor 70, he favors difficult solo trials as the best route to further growth.
characters.name: Jake Thayne

characters.description: Jake's wind-affinity companion and the highest-level member of the party. She joins the group's decision to pause their regular Nevermore progress and pursue individual challenge dungeons.
characters.name: Sylphie

characters.description: The party's healer and plant specialist. She joins the group's decision to pause their regular Nevermore progress and pursue individual challenge dungeons.
characters.name: Dina

characters.description: The party's veteran swordsman. He remains with Jake's group as its members decide to pause their regular Nevermore progress for individual challenge dungeons.
characters.name: Sword Saint

characters.description: A force-and-soul combatant in Jake's Nevermore party. He joins the group's decision to pursue individual challenge dungeons.
characters.name: Fallen King

characters.description: Jake's primordial patron. He monitors the Nevermore run, advises Jake about his fading union oath with Sylphie, and directs him into the Colosseum to settle a wager.
characters.name: Malefic Viper

characters.description: A friendly young spear fighter who registers in the Colosseum alongside Jake. He says his father trained him and appears to be a native participant in the challenge.
characters.name: Owen

characters.description: An elven noblewoman and aspiring sorcerer who approaches Jake after an earlier loss. She offers information, contacts, and practical assistance as he advances.
characters.name: Polly

characters.description: The Colosseum title imposed on Jake after his repeated kick-based victories.
characters.name: Doomfoot

characters.description: The Colosseum official who imposed Jake's Doomfoot title. He oversees advancement, schedules promotion bouts, and confirms rank changes.
characters.name: Battlemaster

characters.description: An unbeaten human martial artist selected as Jake's exceptional promotion opponent. His record and unusual placement mark him as a far greater challenge than the rank normally provides.
characters.name: Benevolent Monk

characters.description: Nevermore's host and the maker of its labyrinth challenge. He watches Jake's unusual Colosseum progress with the Malefic Viper and comments on opponents whose placement exceeds ordinary expectations.
characters.name: Minaga

characters.description: A Valhall-associated entrant whose performance in the Colosseum draws attention from the divine observers monitoring Nevermore.
characters.name: Carmen

characters.description: An undefeated dwarven earth mage selected as Jake's Master Gladiator promotion opponent. He fights with stone defenses, stone spears, and movement through sand.
characters.name: Earthborn Faithful

characters.description: An elven spellblade selected as Jake's bonus Master Gladiator promotion opponent. The image uses light and fire magic and is based on a god of the Altmar Empire.
characters.name: Emberlight Blademaster

characters.description: A Nevermore competitor whose usual fighting style translates poorly to the Colosseum arena.
characters.name: Casper

characters.description: An undefeated Fae illusionist selected for Jake's Warlord promotion match. Her mental and illusion magic conceal a lethal strike, but she has limited physical ability.
characters.name: Living Nightmare

characters.description: A newly C-grade high elf and disciple of Duskleaf who returns to the clan she left behind. She now has enough standing to confront the circumstances of her past on her own terms.
characters.name: Mira

characters.description: The divine authority who explains that Colosseum opponents are system-assisted, level-zero images derived from other beings. He also confirms that selected victors may receive a private message after a match.
characters.name: Worm God

characters.description: Duskleaf's high-elf disciple publicly returns to the Willowwood clan as Mistress Dawnleaf. An Order representative announces that she has claimed the clan.
characters.name: Dawnleaf

characters.description: Dawnleaf's mother, a widowed jeweler supporting three younger children while facing heavy work demands from the Willowwood clan's tax system.
characters.name: Delia

characters.description: A historic Valhall warrior, war god, and Gudrun's husband. His reputation establishes him as an exceptionally powerful figure from humanity's past.
characters.name: Valdemar

characters.description: A spear fighter and meticulous strategist who prepares specialized counters for each opponent. Jake identifies the Valkyrie as Gudrun, Valdemar's wife, during his Champion promotion match.
characters.name: Gudrun

characters.description: One of the seven champions named when Jake gains access to the Gauntlet of the Grand Champion. At this point, the opponent is known only by the Necromancer title.
characters.name: Necromancer

characters.description: The Necromancer is identified as a weakened image of this risen general after killing Jake in their first gauntlet fight.
characters.name: Undying General

characters.description: A champion of shadow magic whom Jake must face during the gauntlet. Her favorable and unfavorable matchups are severe enough to discourage challengers from attempting only part of the sequence.
characters.name: Mistress of Shadows

characters.description: A semi-retired former general and champion who has mastered an extensive range of weapons. Advance research finds no known magic and little dependable information about his full arsenal.
characters.name: Warmaster

characters.description: The Colosseum official is revealed as the retired Warmaster when Jake learns the identity of his final champion opponent.
characters.name: Battlemaster

characters.description: Owen's father and one of the Colosseum's seven champions. Owen asks Jake to defeat him without killing him so that he can return home.
characters.name: Lightning Monarch

characters.description: Polly's former teacher and one of the Colosseum's seven champions. Polly says he forced her into service by threatening her parents and asks Jake to kill his image.
characters.name: Archmage

characters.description: One of the Colosseum's seven champions. Advance research describes her as a beastkin fire mage who also uses illusion magic.
characters.name: Phoenix Queen

characters.description: The shadow champion is identified as Umbra and connected to the Court of Shadows. Her matchup is among the obstacles Jake must consider during the champion gauntlet.
characters.name: Umbra

characters.description: An archer champion selected as Jake's next gauntlet opponent after his fourth victory. At this point, the figure is known only by the Lord of the Hunt title.
characters.name: Lord of the Hunt

characters.description: The hunter champion gives her name as Artemis after surrendering to Jake. She offers him recovery, practical observations about the remaining champions, and limited respect between fellow hunters.
characters.name: Artemis

characters.description: A divine figure who accompanies Artemis to the gathering at Nevermore. Artemis lacks the standing to attend the assembly of primordials without such support.
characters.name: Nature's Attendant

characters.description: An Earth administrator who has spent much of her development on governing and professional work. With integration stabilizing and local responsibilities increasingly delegated, she prepares to focus on combat growth again.
characters.name: Miranda

characters.description: An Earth-side overseer who helps manage construction, integration, and the growing role of freed arrivals. He has recently advanced into C-grade.
characters.name: Hank

characters.description: An empathic Test of Character entrant whose near-perfect result comes from understanding each scenario and guiding its people through empathy, logic, and adaptation.
characters.name: Jacob

characters.description: An analytical competitor whose Test of Character choices are remarkably impartial and consistently benefit the people whose lives he inhabits. His unquestionable result earns the challenge's highest standard reward.
characters.name: Arnold

characters.description: A figure whose plans are targeted by a coordinated deception presenting Valhall and the Malefic Order as hostile factions.
characters.name: Yip of Yore

characters.description: A karma mage and heretic investigating a homeworld whose loyalties appear distorted by false karmic premises. Free from his former controller, he intends to gather proof before leaving.
characters.name: William

characters.description: The Boundless Hydra's chosen, capable of opening wormholes and exploiting weaknesses in spatial barriers. Training intended to control exit points reveals a possible hunger-guided method of navigation.
characters.name: Sandy

characters.description: The sole true royal of her lineage and one of Jake's creations. She plans to leave the Endless Empire for the 93rd universe even though other royals initially fear the danger and political consequences.
characters.name: Vesperia

characters.description: The confidential architect of the House of the Architect. She offers Jake privacy from outside observation and reveals herself as the bound god whose existence sustains the living dungeon.
characters.name: Nevermore

characters.description: An escaped half-elf servant with innate curse energy, ties to a weak resistance group, and intense hatred for his former owner. Jake recruits him as an alchemy student instead of returning him.
characters.name: Half-Elf Servant

characters.description: The half-elf whom Jake recruits as his first formal student. Temlat chooses instruction in alchemy and curse control as a path toward strength and revenge rather than a return to enslavement.
characters.name: Temlat

recaps.ending: The book closes while Jake is still competing in Nevermore. He has completed four challenge dungeons, accumulated an 80 percent combined score multiplier, and entered the Never-Ending Journey as a courier with three lives. His House reward includes a private, time-dilated alchemical domain and ten bound attendants. The Sword Saint has reported a Grand Champion result, but Dina, Sylphie, and the Fallen King remain in separate challenges. Temlat is dead by his own request after destroying his world's ruling order, and Jake has decided against taking another formal student soon. Valdemar's offer of Valhall membership remains unanswered, Artemis still intends a private conversation, and Minaga continues to watch Jake closely. Vesperia has support to travel toward the 93rd universe, while Miranda, William, and Sandy continue their separate preparations and investigations. Neither Jake nor the Malefic Viper understands the origin-linked power that enabled the victory over Valdemar's image.
recaps.in_short: Jake and his party pause their regular Nevermore climb to attempt solo challenge dungeons. In the Colosseum, Jake rises from a restricted level-zero fighter to sole Grand Champion, killing Valdemar's image after an unexplained bloodline survival response. He then completes the Test of Character and Minaga's Endless Labyrinth, while his victories attract Valdemar, Artemis, and many other gods. In the House of the Architect, Jake develops ten varied creations and recruits Temlat as his first student. Temlat evolves into a plague remnant of wrath, destroys his world's oppressive ruling order, then asks Jake to consume him. Jake earns a 20 percent House multiplier and a permanent private alchemical domain, bringing his total challenge multiplier to 80 percent. The book ends as he begins the courier-based Never-Ending Journey with three lives, leaving his party's reunion, divine affiliations, Vesperia's migration, and the nature of his origin power unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne entered Nevermore with Sylphie, Dina, the Sword Saint, and the Fallen King. The group has been advancing through the dungeon while competing for points, with Jake continuing to develop as the Malefic Viper's Chosen.

Jake's party completes floor 70 and reaches another Nevermore City floor while still holding the points record for that stage. Because later floors offer larger rewards and every available challenge dungeon is now open, the five members agree to spend roughly ten internal years on solo trials before reuniting. Jake and the Sword Saint enter the Colosseum, while Dina, Sylphie, and the Fallen King choose different challenges. The Colosseum strips Jake down to a normalized level-zero body, confiscates his equipment, limits his skills, and gives him ten lives. His bloodline, titles, and perception remain active, leaving him unusually capable. He befriends the spear user Owen and meets Polly, an elven sorcerer who offers information. Jake climbs the early ranks without a loss, relying almost entirely on kicks. Experiments with predatory presence become Fear Gaze, a nonlethal technique that can freeze weak opponents and disrupt spell control. The crowd gives him the unwanted name Doomfoot as he approaches the true gladiator ranks.

Jake reaches Gladiator without losing a life and begins weekly ranked bouts, daily show matches, and systematic archery practice. He reveals arcane-enhanced strikes, buys light boots, and continues advancing far faster than ordinary competitors. His promotion to Veteran Gladiator comes through an agreed scoring bout against the Benevolent Monk. Although Jake draws blood first and technically wins, the monk's soul-based defense and attacks leave him convinced that a lethal rematch would be far harder. Jake responds by buying katars and protective equipment suited to his counterattacking style. He also notices Owen hiding lightning magic while Polly develops both magic and basic melee skills. After ten Veteran Gladiator victories, Jake defeats the undefeated dwarven earth mage known as the Earthborn Faithful in his Master Gladiator promotion bout. The opponent surrenders, though the post-match rank notification has not appeared by the end of chapter 16. Jake remains unbeaten with all ten lives intact, while Carmen and the Sword Saint are also noted for strong Colosseum performances.

Jake advances through Warlord and Paragon while refining archery, transmutation, and stable arcane defenses. In a lethal rematch, he defeats the Benevolent Monk after a severe exchange, but an unidentified entity briefly speaks through the dying image and leaves its purpose unclear. Jake then learns that Colosseum opponents are system-assisted level-zero images based on other beings. Owen admits he is the son of one of the champions and has concealed the distinctive lightning inherited from his father. Away from the arena, Mira returns to the Willowwood clan with the authority of Duskleaf's disciple. Publicly revealed as Mistress Dawnleaf, she claims the clan to protect it and reunites with her mother Delia and three younger siblings. She refuses to rule their choices and instead arranges formal status, protection, and freedom of movement. Back in the Colosseum, Jake completes ten Paragon victories and prepares for his promotion to Champion with his archery still largely concealed.

Jake's Champion promotion opponent is Gudrun, the Valhallian Valkyrie and Valdemar's wife. Her formations, prepared equipment, and deceptive tactics initially control the arena, but Jake reveals his bow, wounds her at range, defeats her in melee, and grants her requested warrior's death. Champion rank opens the Gauntlet of the Grand Champion against seven other champions. Owen asks Jake to spare his father, the Lightning Monarch, while Polly asks him to kill the Archmage who coerced her through threats against her parents. Jake exhausts the Lightning Monarch's enhancement and persuades him to surrender, leaving Owen with an unwanted expectation of succession. He then kills the Archmage's image with a prepared arrow barrage. Jake's third opponent is the heavily armored Necromancer. His opening plan pierces and blasts apart the champion's armor, but the death knight survives the apparent killing wound. By the end of chapter 32, Jake is poisoned and injured as the unresolved first fight continues through spreading miasma.

The Undying General kills Jake in their first gauntlet fight, costing him one life, but Jake returns with a plan and destroys the image in their rematch. He then defeats the Phoenix Queen after her apparently fatal loss triggers a fiery reconstruction and she surrenders while weakened. Jake fights the Lord of the Hunt in a prolonged archery duel and wins by cutting her bowstring with a concealed final arrow. She identifies herself as Artemis, recovers her divine memories, and offers Jake limited hunting instruction after he declines her invitation to become her chosen. Jake then faces Umbra in a shadow-favored arena. His bloodline perception defeats her concealment, clones, and shadow domain, and she surrenders after warning him about the reigning Grand Champion. Jake's last gauntlet opponent is the Battlemaster, revealed as the retired Warmaster. The weapon master cycles through legendary armor, traps, explosives, and a broad arsenal, but Jake turns the wire trap against him and forces a surrender. Jake becomes a Grand Champion with nine lives remaining. He may now leave, accept escalating show matches, or challenge the Warrior for sole status. Based on the title and the available warnings, Jake believes the final opponent is Valdemar.

Jake challenges Valdemar's image and spends repeated lives learning an opponent whose direct axe attacks cannot be safely blocked. Valdemar retains divine memories and explains that recognition, surrender, or death may end the match. On Jake's final life, an unstable arcane body boost lets him inflict serious wounds, and Fear Gaze creates an opening that earns Valdemar's recognition. The intended challenge is already cleared, but Valdemar still brings down a final overwhelming strike. Jake releases a suppressed survival response from his bloodline. For several seconds he gains extraordinary control, creates a void, converts sand into usable energy, and coordinates a fatal counterattack. Valdemar dies, and Jake becomes the sole Grand Champion. The Colosseum awards a 25 percent score multiplier, a powerful title, and an emblem for normalized virtual duels. The bloodline episode then leaves Jake's senses badly distorted. The Sword Saint separately becomes a Grand Champion by defeating Umbra, but his transcendence backlash persists, and he cannot clear Valdemar.

The Malefic Viper cannot fully explain Jake's victory, though he suspects Jake briefly released a normally suppressed bloodline state and spent accumulated origin energy to survive it. Artemis and the true Valdemar begin traveling to Nevermore after receiving records of their images. Jake partially recovers and enters the Test of Character, a sequence of scenarios in which he may guide or take control of another person's body. He responds according to his own judgment, sometimes refusing to intervene and sometimes removing threats directly. During the trial his senses recover, his archery improves, and Fear Gaze becomes the mythical Primal Gaze of the Apex Hunter.
